messages.subject: example of creating extensions?
parts:
Hi,

The documentation for writing extensions is very nice. However I find it hard to grasp the details of creating extensions. Would it be possible to add a very simple, but complete, extension example to the docs?

1. Lets say I wanted to create a meanTrim function that takes a vector as argument and trims off the min and max values first. i.e.

meanTrim <- function(x) {
  x <- x[x != max(x)]
  x <- x[x != min(x)]
  return(mean(x))
}

# Example:
vec <- c(2.3, 2.7, 3.1, 4.9, 1.0, 2.4, 2.6, 2.1, 2.0, 1.9)
print(mean(vec))
print(meanTrim(vec))


2. A more involved example would be something where I have a java class that does something useful and i want to take advantage of that in an  R function

e.g. i have the Java class
public class StringTransformer {
  
  /** strips off any non numeric char from the string. */
  public static String toNumber(String txt) {
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    txt.chars().mapToObj( i -> (char)i )
    .filter( c -> Character.isDigit(c) ).forEach( c -> result.append(c) );
    return result.toString();
  }
  
}  

and I want to make a library which has a function called makeNumeric which uses the StringTransformer.toNumber() functionality.

3. Lets say i want to override (mask) existing functionality .e.g i want to override library() with something that guesses the correct package so i can do e.g. library("dplyr") and get the same thing as if I would have written library("org.renjin.cran:dplyr"), what do i need to do to make that happen?

If you answer here, I'd be happy to type up a tutorial and submit a patch suggestion to the docs.

Best regards,
Per

messages.author: 101bcf2abc4700dc
messages.subject: Re: example of creating extensions?
parts:
Hi Per,

You refer to documentation part about writing Renjin extensions. 

<1>
  • create files src/main/R/meantrim.R and src/test/R/test.meantrim.R
    • in meanTrim.R write your function:
      meanTrim <- function(x) {

• x <- x[x != max(x)]
      x <- x[x != min(x)]

• mean(x)
      }
    • in test.meantrim.R write your tests using Renjins hamcrest package:
      library("com.mydomain:meantrim")
      library("hamcrest")
      assertThat(meanTrim(1:10), identicalTo(5.5))
  • create the NAMESPACE file and export your function
    export(meanTrim)
  • copy the example po.xml and change the groupId and artefactId to "com.mydomain" and "meantrim", respectively.
  • your extension/package folder should now look like this:
    pom.xml
    NAMESPACE
    src
    |-- main
    |    |-- R
    |        |- meantrim.R
    |-- test
         |-- R
             |- test.meantrim.R  
  • now you can do "mvn test" to test your package and "mvn package" to create the fat binary jar file from your package which will be stored in your "target" folder
  • you can now import this package in your Renjin session and use it

<2> following the documentation about importing java classes: http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/importing-java-classes-in-r-code.html
  • create src/main/java/
    • create StringTransformer.java:
      package transformers;
      public class StringTransformer {

•   public static String toNumber(String txt) {
          StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
          txt.chars().mapToObj(i -> (char) i)
            .filter(c -> Character.isDigit(c))
            .forEach(c -> result.append(c));
          return result.toString();
        }
      }

• add extractDigits function (to your meantrim.R file):
    • extractDigits <- function(x) {
          import(transformers.StringTransformer)
          sapply(x, function(txt) StringTransformer$toNumber(txt = txt), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
      }
      makeNumber <- function(x) as.numeric(extractDigits(x))
    • add test case to test.meantrim.R file:
      assertThat(extractDigits(c("5", "6Y8", "He", "02")), identicalTo(c("5", "68", "", "02")))
      assertThat(makeNumber(c("5", "6Y8", "He", "02")), identicalTo(c(5, 68, NA, 2)))
  • export the new functions in your NAMESPACE and use mvn to test and package your extension
<3> depending on whether you want to do this inside your package or java application, you need to have a list of CRAN and BioConductor package names and depending in which list the input name resides add to correct prefix to the input and pass that to base::library()

If you want to do it in your application follow the instructions here: http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/library/evaluating.html

Kind regards,
Parham

Any suggestions?

Best regards,
Per

      meanTrim <- function(x) {
      x <- x[x != max(x)]
      x <- x[x != min(x)]
      mean(x)
      }
    • in test.meantrim.R write your tests using Renjins hamcrest package:
      library("com.mydomain:meantrim")
      library("hamcrest")
      assertThat(meanTrim(1:10), identicalTo(5.5))
  • create the NAMESPACE file and export your function
    export(meanTrim)
  • copy the example po.xml and change the groupId and artefactId to "com.mydomain" and "meantrim", respectively.
  • your extension/package folder should now look like this:
    pom.xml
    NAMESPACE
    src
    |-- main
    |    |-- R
    |        |- meantrim.R
    |-- test
         |-- R
             |- test.meantrim.R  
  • now you can do "mvn test" to test your package and "mvn package" to create the fat binary jar file from your package which will be stored in your "target" folder
  • you can now import this package in your Renjin session and use it

<2> following the documentation about importing java classes: http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/importing-java-classes-in-r-code.html
  • create src/main/java/
    • create StringTransformer.java:
      package transformers;
      public class StringTransformer {
        public static String toNumber(String txt) {
          StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
          txt.chars().mapToObj(i -> (char) i)
            .filter(c -> Character.isDigit(c))
            .forEach(c -> result.append(c));
          return result.toString();
        }
      }
  • add extractDigits function (to your meantrim.R file):
    • extractDigits <- function(x) {
          import(transformers.StringTransformer)
          sapply(x, function(txt) StringTransformer$toNumber(txt = txt), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
      }
      makeNumber <- function(x) as.numeric(extractDigits(x))
    • add test case to test.meantrim.R file:
      assertThat(extractDigits(c("5", "6Y8", "He", "02")), identicalTo(c("5", "68", "", "02")))
      assertThat(makeNumber(c("5", "6Y8", "He", "02")), identicalTo(c(5, 68, NA, 2)))
  • export the new functions in your NAMESPACE and use mvn to test and package your extension
<3> depending on whether you want to do this inside your package or java application, you need to have a list of CRAN and BioConductor package names and depending in which list the input name resides add to correct prefix to the input and pass that to base::library()

If you want to do it in your application follow the instructions here: http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/library/evaluating.html
